Business E2E map

Personas, user journeys and the feature catalog of Bunkai TMS.

Overview

Bunkai TMS is a multi-tenant test management product. QA engineers, QA leads, developers and autonomous agents author acceptance test cases (ATCs) tied to user stories, group them into plans, execute runs, file bugs and read traceability and coverage. The staging OpenAPI lists 79 paths and 102 operations. The app has 38 UI routes plus the public /qa testability page.

Role hierarchy

Roles on a workspace member: viewer < member < admin < owner (MemberRole, lib/types.ts). Member status: active, invited, suspended. Personal access tokens carry capabilities atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin (lib/api/capabilities.ts); a cookie session holds all four.

Permissionviewermemberadminowner
Read projects, ATCs, runs, bugsyesyesyesyes
Author ATCs, run tests, file bugsno (to verify)yesyesyes
Invite and manage members, tokens at workspace levelnonoyesyes
Billing, delete workspacenonoto verifyyes

The matrix is inferred from the role ladder and the legacy RBAC table; the exact per-endpoint gate is not re-verified here (see discovery-gaps).

Top journeys by risk: execute a run (core value), author an ATC (the anchoring rule), upgrade billing (revenue), invite a teammate (security).

Persona: QA engineer (member)

System role member (evidence: MemberRole). Goal: write ATCs fast, execute them and file bugs with evidence. Pain points seen in validation: titles must be 3 to 200 characters, an ATC needs at least 1 step and at least 1 acceptance criterion, at most 10 tags (lib/atcs/validation.ts). Test-account keys: STAGING_USER_EMAIL (the one authenticating account, owner in its own workspace; switch to the admin or viewer workspace seeded by BK-337 to exercise those roles) and STAGING_MEMBER_EMAIL (present in .env, does not authenticate on staging as of 2026-09-18). Journeys: author an ATC, execute a run, report a bug.

Persona: QA lead (admin or owner)

System roles admin and owner. Goal: see coverage, milestone progress, bug heatmap and recovery cycles, manage the team and the plan tier. Reaches /home, /projects/[slug]/metrics, /traceability, /milestones, /settings/billing, /workspaces/[id]/members. Test accounts: STAGING_USER_EMAIL in the owner workspace or the BK-337 admin workspace. Journeys: invite a teammate, upgrade billing, read traceability.

Persona: viewer

System role viewer. Read-only stakeholder. Test account: the bk337-viewer-role-qa workspace reachable from STAGING_USER_EMAIL (AGENTS.md section 13.1). Write attempts should be refused; the exact refusal codes are not mapped yet (discovery-gaps).

Persona: autonomous test agent and CI

Not a member role: a caller holding a personal access token (bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>) with a subset of the four capabilities. Runs carry executor_mode human, agent or ci. A PAT cannot mint another PAT: minting needs a cookie session. Journeys: execute a run, issue a token.

Journey: first-time setup

Entry: /login. Persona: QA engineer, new owner.

  1. Sign in by email-first form (POST /api/v1/auth/check-email), password sign-in (/auth/signin) or magic link (/auth/magic-link); OAuth lands at /auth/oauth/[provider] then /auth/callback. Signup uses /auth/signup and /auth/confirm (email confirmation), /auth/resend re-sends it. Password minimum is 8.
  2. /onboarding bootstraps the first workspace (POST /api/v1/workspaces).
  3. /projects/new creates a project (POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/projects).
  4. Build the module tree, add stories and acceptance criteria, then author the first ATC.

Branches: unconfirmed email blocks sign-in; unauthenticated visits to /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity redirect to /login?next=.... External-dependency step: magic link and email confirmation need a mailbox, not automatable in a spec without a mail hook. Data: see business-data-context entities; API: see business-api-context auth-model.

Journey: author an ATC

Entry: a project page, then /atcs/new or /tests/new. Persona: QA engineer.

  1. Create modules (POST /projects/{id}/modules) and stories (POST /modules/{id}/user-stories; story status draft or ready_to_test). Stories can be imported from Jira (POST /api/v1/imports, job status queued, running, completed, failed).
  2. Add acceptance criteria to the story (POST /user-stories/{id}/acceptance-criteria).
  3. Create the ATC (POST /api/v1/atcs): title, layer (UI, API, Unit), optional technique and priority, steps, tags, and at least one acceptance criterion id.
  4. Edit (PATCH /atcs/{id}), duplicate (/atcs/{id}/duplicate), tag (PUT /tests/{id}/tags), reorder, search (/atcs/search, /search), export (/projects/{id}/atcs/export).

Failure points: no steps, no acceptance criterion, title out of range, more than 10 tags: all rejected by validation. Entities: entities. Endpoints: business-api-context journey-author-atc. Features: feature-authoring.

Journey: execute a run

Entry: /projects/[slug]/runs or a test page. Personas: QA engineer, agent, CI.

  1. Create the run (POST /api/v1/runs) with executor_mode human, agent or ci.
  2. Mark each step passed, failed or blocked (POST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark).
  3. Finish with verdict passed or failed (/runs/{id}/finish) or abort (/runs/{id}/abort). An inactivity sweep also closes stale runs (migration 0075).
  4. A failed step leads to a bug; the project run report is GET /projects/{id}/runs/report; per-test history is GET /tests/{id}/runs.

Run completion notifications exist (migration 0066). State machine: business-data-context state-run.

Journey: report and triage a bug

Entry: /projects/[slug]/bugs. Create (POST /api/v1/bugs): title 5 to 200 characters, severity P1 to P4, evidence capped. Status ladder open, in_progress, resolved, closed (POST /bugs/{id}/status); assign with /bugs/{id}/assign. The heatmap is GET /projects/{id}/bugs/heatmap. Bugs notify through the workspace notifications and the daily digest.

Journey: invite a teammate

Entry: /workspaces/[id]/members (admin or owner). Issue (POST /workspaces/{id}/invites), rotate or revoke (POST|DELETE /workspaces/{id}/invites/{inviteId}); the invitee opens /invites/accept (POST /invites/accept). Seat caps apply: Community allows 5 seats. Invite tokens are single-use secrets (lib/api/invite-tokens.ts). The invite email depends on Resend. Members can leave (DELETE /workspaces/{id}/membership).

Journey: upgrade the plan

Entry: /settings/billing then /settings/billing/upgrade. Tiers: community, cloud, enterprise (PLAN_TIERS: Community 5 seats, 3 projects, 30 days retention, free; Enterprise unlimited). Checkout (POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout) uses Stripe with a seat quantity bounded by active members and the Cloud seat cap; /billing/checkout/cancel abandons it. External-dependency step: Stripe hosted checkout is not automatable end to end. Failure: seat quantity below active members or above the cap returns seat_quantity_invalid.

Journey: read traceability and coverage

Entry: /projects/[slug]/traceability, /metrics, /milestones, the workspace /home dashboard. Reads: GET /projects/{id}/traceability (story to criterion to ATC), /coverage, /metrics/recovery-cycles, workspace /coverage, /open-bugs, /active-runs, /recent-projects. Milestones group runs (POST /projects/{id}/milestones).

Journey: issue an API token

Entry: /settings/tokens. POST /api/v1/tokens returns the secret once; scopes are the four capabilities. Revoke with DELETE /tokens/{id}. Cookie session only: a PAT cannot create a PAT. Used by CI and agents (bun run api:login in this repo mints one).

Cross-feature flow: plan, run, bug, milestone

A test plan (POST /projects/{id}/test-plans, tests added through /test-plans/{id}/tests) selects ATCs. Runs execute them, optionally under a milestone and an environment (/projects/{id}/environments). A failed step feeds a bug whose status shows in the home dashboard and the digest. Metrics and traceability read all four. A change in any ATC step changes what the next run executes, so plan membership is the handoff point to test.

Feature flags and WIP

No feature-flag mechanism was found in the e2e scan. STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is optional: without it checkout is unavailable. The roadmap files in the target repo (docs/) list planned work; they were not read for this map.

Discovery gaps

  • Per-endpoint role gate (which of viewer, member, admin, owner may call each operation) was not verified; the matrix in overview is inferred.
  • STAGING_MEMBER_*, STAGING_ADMIN_*, STAGING_OWNER_* do not authenticate on staging (measured 2026-09-18); roles are exercised through workspace switching on one account.
  • Frontend form-level validation messages were not collected; only backend schemas.
  • Roadmap and planned features in the target docs/ were not read; flags-wip is therefore thin.
  • Module depth cap (6) comes from the legacy data map and was not re-measured.
  • Journeys were traced from route files and the OpenAPI spec, not replayed in a browser this session.
  • The data map has no workspace lifecycle state machine; workspace state is described under business-data-context entity-workspaces.
  • Legacy markdown (May 2026) covered 8 operations and 8 migrations; the product now has 102 operations and 88 migration files, so legacy content was used only for personas and journeys wording.
